key_insight: FracGen learns physically plausible fracture video generation from a single intact image by conditioning on dense physics signals so it can predict how objects deform, crack, and tear.
engineering_relevance: The method offers controllable, material-aware fracture prediction that could support faster virtual testing, design exploration, and damage visualization without expensive per-scene simulation.
method: Builds FracSim, a simulation pipeline that combines MPM with a continuum damage model to generate paired fracture videos and dense physical fields.
Trains FracGen to jointly predict RGB video and physical maps, forcing the model to represent underlying mechanics rather than only appearance.
Uses physics-informed losses to keep predicted fracture fields mutually consistent and controllable during generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a new benchmark for physical plausibility and states that experiments show FracGen outperforms prior video generation baselines in both physical and visual fidelity.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality simulated fracture-field supervision, so real-world transfer and robustness to unseen materials or loading conditions may still be challenging.
paper_title: FracGen: Learning How Objects Stretch and Tear with Physics-Informed Video Generation
